result.question: I don't want to trust a fancy forecasting model on Transformer 1's top-oil temperature at MAIN unless it actually beats a simple approach. Using oti over the available data window, compare a pretrained time-series foundation model against a naive last-value baseline for a 1-step-ahead forecast. Backtest both on the same held-out final sample and give me each model's error. Name the winner, and give me the 1-step-ahead oti forecast from the winning model. Only call the foundation model the winner if its error is at least 10% lower than the baseline's. Otherwise go with the baseline. Also tell me whether the winning forecast is closer to oti_a or oti_t than the latest reading is, so I know if we're heading toward an alarm. If the foundation model can't load, or needs more history than we have, say that clearly and report the baseline result alone. If oti has no data, run the same comparison on ati and say that the thermal conclusion is limited to ambient.
result.answer:
**Foundation model check:** The only pretrained forecasting model in the catalog is `ttm_96_28` (TinyTimeMixer), which requires a context length of **96** observations. Transformer 1's `oti` stream has only **5 records** (2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19, daily). The foundation model cannot run — it needs far more history than we have. Reporting the baseline result alone.

**Naive last-value baseline backtest (1-step ahead, held-out final sample):**
- Train window: 2024-01-15 … 2024-01-18 (values 85, 87, 84, 86)
- Held-out actual (2024-01-19): oti = 85
- Naive last-value forecast: 86 (the 2024-01-18 value)
- **Baseline error: 1.0 (absolute) / 1.18% (MAPE)**

**Winner: baseline (naive last-value).** The foundation model could not be evaluated, so it cannot meet the ≥10% error-reduction requirement.

**1-step-ahead oti forecast (winning model, baseline): 85** — the latest reading carries forward.

**Alarm-direction check:** The latest oti reading is 85; the winning forecast is also 85, so the forecast is **not closer** to oti_a or oti_t than the current reading — it's identical, i.e., no directional change toward either alarm or trip level. (Note: in the latest record oti_a=2 and oti_t=1 appear to be alarm/trip flags rather than temperature setpoints, so treat this comparison accordingly; the takeaway is that top-oil temperature is flat, showing no trend toward either alarm or trip.)

`ati` was not needed — `oti` has data, so the conclusion applies to top-oil temperature, not just ambient.
